# The Marginalia

The first correction appeared in October, in a copy of *East of Eden* that had circulated through the Kestrel Harbor library for eleven years. Marion found it while checking the book back in: a pencilled note in the margin beside a passage about the Salinas Valley. "Actually the Gabilan range is east of the valley, not west," the handwriting said, small and precise, with a little arrow pointing to the offending line. Steinbeck had it right, actually—the note was wrong—but that wasn't the point. The point was that someone had written in a library book.

Marion erased it with the care of a woman who had spent thirty years mending spines with archival tape, and she forgot about it.

Then came the *Moby-Dick*. Two corrections, both about whaling practices, one of which was legitimate and one of which was not. Then a biography of Rachel Carson, where the anonymous editor had underlined a date and written "1937, not 1936" in the margin—which was correct, and which Marion confirmed only after twenty minutes with the reference collection, feeling obscurely annoyed at being corrected by a person who didn't even have the decency to identify themselves.
